clinical_scope.population: Adults and young people aged 16 years or older unless otherwise specified by local protocol
excluded_populations: pediatric specialty pathways unless explicitly validated
clinical_scope.intended_use: High-risk candidate retrieval and guideline-based verification for suspected Acute Myocardial Infarction.
clinical_scope.important_boundary: This graph supports clinical reasoning and missed-diagnosis risk reduction; it is not an autonomous diagnostic system.

distinctions.description: AMI is ACS with acute myocardial injury and ischemic evidence, while ACS also includes unstable angina without troponin-defined myocardial injury.

basic_info.working_definition: Acute myocardial infarction is acute myocardial injury, usually detected by a rise and/or fall of cardiac troponin, with clinical evidence of acute myocardial ischemia.
why_high_risk_for_missed_diagnosis: Chest pain can be absent or atypical, especially in older adults, women, and people with diabetes or chronic kidney disease.
Symptoms may present as dyspnea, epigastric discomfort, nausea, diaphoresis, syncope, fatigue, or heart failure.
Early ECG may be nondiagnostic and initial troponin may be negative if measured too early.
Aortic dissection, pulmonary embolism, pericarditis, pneumothorax, and gastrointestinal disease can mimic AMI.
basic_info.time_sensitivity: Time-critical evaluation for STEMI reperfusion eligibility and high-risk NSTEMI invasive management.
do_not_use_as: a replacement for serial troponin protocols

case_input_normalization.single_pass_missing_information_policy: Do not ask follow-up questions. Mark missing critical information explicitly and state how missingness affects verification.
case_input_normalization.normalization_patch_note: Normalization rules were systematized on 2026-06-28 to support retrieval from textual triggers, abbreviations, and numeric clinical facts. Rules map common case expressions to graph node ids where available. They are retrieval signals, not autonomous diagnostic criteria.

activation_logic.minimum_activation: Compatible ischemic symptom or equivalent plus cardiac risk context, abnormal ECG, troponin abnormality, or hemodynamic complication.

strong_activation_patterns.reason: Potential STEMI requiring immediate reperfusion pathway.
Meets core myocardial infarction verification concept if acute ischemia is present.

symptom_to_candidate_retrieval.scoring_warning: Weights are for retrieval and explanation only. They are not calibrated probabilities and must not be used as a diagnostic score.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Does the case include ischemic chest discomfort or an ischemic equivalent?
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Lower priority but do not exclude atypical AMI.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Presentation cannot be characterized; list missing symptom quality, onset, duration, and associated features.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is a 12-lead ECG available and is there STEMI-equivalent or ischemic change?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Classify possible STEMI/NSTEMI and activate appropriate pathway.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: If nondiagnostic and symptoms persist, repeat ECG and continue troponin pathway.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Critical missing data: ECG not provided.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is there a rise/fall of cardiac troponin above the 99th percentile?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Supports acute myocardial injury; require ischemic evidence to label MI.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Early negative troponin does not exclude AMI; follow serial protocol.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Critical missing data: serial troponin timing/results.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Does myocardial injury occur with ischemic symptoms, ischemic ECG, imaging evidence, or coronary thrombus?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Classify as acute myocardial infarction if criteria align.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Consider non-ischemic myocardial injury or type 2 injury.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Cannot distinguish AMI from myocardial injury without ischemic evidence.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is this STEMI, NSTEMI, or uncertain AMI subtype?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Use subtype to determine urgency and pathway.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: If uncertain, continue ACS evaluation and evaluate mimics.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Subtype cannot be assigned without ECG/troponin.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Are shock, heart failure, arrhythmia, mechanical complication, or cardiac arrest present?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Escalate to critical care/cath team as locally indicated.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Could aortic dissection, PE, pericarditis, pneumothorax, or GI catastrophe better explain the presentation?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Report competing diagnoses and avoid harmful premature treatment.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: AMI remains more likely if ischemic evidence dominates.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Differential incomplete; list missing red-flag data.

distinguishing_features: Ischemic symptoms without troponin-defined myocardial injury may represent unstable angina.
Requires ACS pathway despite no AMI confirmation.
Abrupt tearing chest/back pain, pulse deficit, neurologic symptoms, mediastinal widening, or hypotension may mimic AMI.
Antithrombotic therapy can be dangerous if dissection is missed.
Pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea, syncope, hypoxemia, VTE risk factors.
Troponin may be elevated from RV strain.
Positional pleuritic pain, diffuse ST elevation/PR depression, viral prodrome.
Troponin can be elevated in myocarditis.
Sudden pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea with unilateral breath-sound changes.
Severe chest pain after vomiting, sepsis, subcutaneous emphysema.

final_assessment.safety_statement: Clinical decision support only; urgent clinician assessment is required when a high-risk condition is suspected.

evidence_sources.title: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes
evidence_sources.publisher: American College of Cardiology / American Heart Association and partner societies
key_points: Addresses acute management across unstable angina, NSTEMI, and STEMI.
Supports rapid ECG-based classification, serial cardiac troponin evaluation, risk stratification, and timely reperfusion or invasive management when indicated.

evidence_sources.title: 2023 ESC Guidelines for the management of acute coronary syndromes
key_points: Provides an integrated guideline for patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome across the spectrum of STEMI and NSTE-ACS.
Used here for diagnostic classification and high-risk ACS verification logic.

evidence_sources.title: Fourth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction (2018)
key_points: Myocardial infarction requires acute myocardial injury detected by cardiac troponin rise and/or fall plus clinical evidence of acute myocardial ischemia.
Acute myocardial injury without ischemic evidence should not automatically be labeled myocardial infarction.

must_not: Do not make an autonomous definitive diagnosis.
Do not use a single symptom, sign, laboratory result, score, or imaging clue as a standalone rule-in or rule-out criterion.
Do not provide patient-facing reassurance when critical red-flag data are missing.
Do not ignore competing high-risk differential diagnoses.
Do not replace local emergency, specialty, or hospital protocols.
Do not generate medication orders; recommend clinician-led pathway activation instead.
Do not diagnose AMI from troponin elevation alone without ischemic evidence.
Do not exclude AMI using a single early negative troponin.
Do not ignore aortic dissection red flags before antithrombotic assumptions.
must_do: Use this graph for candidate retrieval, missed-diagnosis risk reduction, and guideline-based verification.
Separate supporting evidence, evidence against, and missing critical information.
State whether verification is complete, partial, impossible from available data, or contradicted.
Include differential diagnoses that can mimic the condition.
Trace guideline-dependent claims to evidence IDs.
Mark output as clinical decision support requiring qualified clinician review.
Always require ECG status and serial troponin status for verification.
Always distinguish AMI from unstable angina and non-ischemic myocardial injury.
